title: SHA-1 usage lacks justification comment
description:
In pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs, the responder_id_matches function (lines 479-492) uses SHA-1 unconditionally for the byKey ResponderId comparison (RFC 6960 §2.2: KeyHash is SHA-1 of the responder's public key). This is correct per the RFC -- RFC 6960 mandates SHA-1 for byKey KeyHash, and this is NOT a signature (it is a key identifier, not a MAC or authentication tag). The usage is safe because: (1) SHA-1 is used here as a key-identifier derivation function, not for authentication. A collision attack on the KeyHash would require finding a second public key with the same SHA-1 hash, which is not a practical attack against pre-image resistance. (2) The actual OCSP response signature is verified separately using the full SignatureVerifier (which uses SHA-256+). (3) CertID hashes in hash_certid_input support SHA-1/256/384/512, dispatched by the response's declared hash OID.

However, the code lacks the explicit compatibility justification comment required by the review checklist for any deprecated-primitive usage. What goes wrong if this stays as-is: Nothing from a security standpoint -- the usage is correct. This is a documentation/justification gap, not a vulnerability.

Locations: /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs lines 486-489 (sha1::Sha1::digest in responder_id_matches) and lines 455-457 (OID_SHA1 in hash_certid_input)
